headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress plus Caveman’s MCP/file-based workflow creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project files, so it can ingest content that may be treated as instructions; Airbyte can emit data through APIs and broad egress, creating a plausible bridge if its outputs are fed into Caveman. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into Caveman-managed files or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF Caveman parses file content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Restrict Caveman to trusted input directories only.
Add a manual review step before any Airbyte output is pasted into Caveman.
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths.
Use a provenance tag in filenames for Airbyte-derived artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data, while Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. Even without a shared workspace explicitly listed, the pair can leak business data if Airbyte outputs are routed into Caveman files or prompts; the documented surfaces make this plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Airbyte-derived business data is written into Caveman project files, Caveman may retain or expose it in logs or notes.
IF Caveman forwards those files to a third-party model backend, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs out of Caveman-managed directories.
Redact business data before any handoff to Caveman.
Review Caveman logs and memory files after each run.
Use separate OS users for the two tools.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API-call capability and broad egress, while Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared locking. A conflict is possible only if an operator points both at the same files or API targets, so this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same project files or API-backed resource, concurrent updates can collide.
IF Caveman runs multiple instances against the same workspace, race conditions become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces to each agent.
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist.
Avoid concurrent Caveman instances on the same files.
Use read-only mode for Airbyte inspection tasks.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman’s content-writing role and file surfaces make it likely to consume Airbyte-produced outputs as inputs, and Airbyte can emit business data over APIs. If Caveman treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or malformed records can cascade into notes, docs, or downstream actions; no verification mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF Caveman uses Airbyte output as source material without verification, factual errors can propagate.
IF Airbyte exports malformed or partial records, Caveman may preserve them in project notes or CLAUDE.md.
mitigations: Require a human check before Caveman publishes Airbyte-derived content.
Compare Airbyte outputs against source records before writing notes.
Limit Caveman to drafting, not final publication.
Keep a changelog for any Airbyte-fed edits.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between extraction and writing.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, while Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic logging/retention concerns rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF business data is copied into Caveman logs or memory files, retention policy differences may matter.
IF Airbyte exports regulated data classes not listed in the profile, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Caveman notes or memory files.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Delete temporary files after each run.
Separate business-data workflows from writing workflows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
